reviews.title: SCAM INTERFACE & DECEPTIVE BILLING!!
reviews.text: Do not download this app. They run deceptive web ads offering a "$1 one-week trial," but the moment you sign up, they sneakily enroll you in an overlapping $20 monthly subscription on the exact same day. It's a complete billing trap designed to charge your credit card twice at the same time. Once you figure out their trick, it's too late. I'm in the process of disputing now and it's so much work for no reason. Even worse, they bypass Apple's native subscription menu so you can't easily cancel it in your iPhone settings. Please stay far FAR away from this app. Complete scam, avoid at all costs!

reviews.title: A $20 Glow-Up & a Free Sexuality Change
reviews.text:
Accidentally downloaded this thinking it was QOVES. Unfortunately, I was $20in by the time I learned that my face could apparently be improved by becoming leaner, more masculine, more gym-obsessed, and, most impressively, heterosexual.

The "10/10 life" feature was the real masterpiece, According to the app, my ideal future involves helicopters, yachts, rooftop parties, tech-bro conference energy, and a rotating cast of conventionally attractive women.

Tiny issue: I'm gay.

Which would have been very easy to account for if the app had asked literally one more question before generating an entire fantasy life around a very specific straight-male ideal

That’s really the bigger problem. The analysis feels generic, the recommendations are heavily rooted in looksmaxing/manosphere aesthetics, and its definition of the "ideal man" seems suspiciously narrow: more angular, more muscular, more status-coded, more conventionally masculine, and apparently surrounded by women at all times.

A few of the facial observations were genuinely useful, so I can’t quite justify only 1 star. The 2nd star is mostly for the accidental comedy value of watching the app construct an entire "10/10 life" for me around gym culture, status symbols, attractive women, and an apparently mandatory heterosexual awakening.

reviews.title: Not helpful for women, but okay. AI so limited
reviews.text: There's lots of genuinely useful material here, and I think it will most helpful for men. For one, as a girl, the advice seems really basic. Change your pillowcase, switch to silk/satin, use Vitamin C for skin evenness. Also, since it's powered by AI, there's only so much it can tell you as far as flattering outfits or hairstyles go --- all your suggestions will be for a straight haired white girl or your typical afro/3-4 level coils in a bob. Ex. my hair is 2c, none of their haircut suggestions made any sense. Also no real color analysis hair or makeup or clothing wise. Super super basic. As for outfits, I didn't find it useful, and women are probably more familiar with Kibbe/flattering fits than an AI app could ever be. I probably would have given this a 3/5 if it weren't for the double charge. 9.99 once for facial analysis, and AGAIN for hair/outfits. That's just greedy! And definitely not a service worth $20! I'd say, if you're a man who knows nothing about self care, yes, this may be worth 20 for you. If you're an average lady, no. There's nothing new here.

reviews.title: Overpriced ChatGPT
reviews.text:
Very briefly took a look at this app. Took a halt when I discovered there are virtually NO features that are for free. You have the option to pay $10 A WEEK, or a $50 yearly subscription that comes out to .45 cents a day. 

The only 'free' feature is an option to make your own tasks, which I can do on my iphone if I really cared (again for free). Even still, the tasks are counterproductive if you don't have the 'tailored' advice given via the report that you have to pay for. The report, facial analysis, style analysis, and AI chat are all subscription based services that are extremely overpriced for something that I can easily put into Chat GPT at no cost. 

I ask the developers: what exactly makes your app any more valuable than what Chat GPT can provide? What are you adding to this market - aside from profiting off of insecure men under the guise of self-help improvement. Yes, companies profit off of people's insecurities all the time, but at least they TRY to be subtle about it. $10 a week - totaling an average of $40 a month is ludicrous. Planet Fitness is cheaper and I get access to a tanning bed. Hell, the YMCA is $30 and I get access to a fkn POOL. 

I wanted something a little more creative than the typical AI slop. Maybe something more data oriented. Who knows, maybe you actually DO get solid feedback on this app. But how the hell would I know because there's no access to a preview. I cannot trust this will provide solid improvements & I am not willing to dish out $50 to figure out if it is. Make it free and I'll reconsider.
